T he stage is set for the INDIA bloc’s mega rally at Delhi’s Ramlila Maidan on Sunday (November 1, 2026), with opposition leaders and supporters from different states beginning to reach the national capital for a show of strength against alleged electoral irregularities and to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The bloc carried out a symbolic “public impeachment” of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, unanimously adopting a motion by a show of hands on Saturday (October 31). They levelled six charges against him, including conspiring with the ruling BJP to steal elections, deleting 13.2 crore voters through the special intensive revision (SIR) of voter lists, and acting at the behest of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah. Opposition parties in West Bengal have stepped up the heat on the issue of 16.10 lakh appeals filed against the inclusion of voters following the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) in the State. Leaders of the Mamata All India Trinamool Congress and the Communist Party of India (Marxist) have questioned the lack of clarity over who authorised the filing of the appeals after the SIR concluded in the State. Opposition in West Bengal questions ECI over 16.10 lakh voter-inclusion appeals amid accountability concerns and SIR controversy. Union Minister Hardeep Singh Puri on Saturday said INDIA bloc’s upcoming rally in Delhi is a “serious political mistake” and asked Congress leader Rahul Gandhi to “introspect”. Mr. Puri called the INDIA bloc’s Sunday (November 1) rally as “completely insensitive to the mass atrocities committed 42 years ago”. He noted that the trading community has also urged the Congress to reconsider the date of the rally in view of the festive season. Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Saturday (October 31) met Trinamool Congress supremo Mamata Banerjee in Delhi and thanked her for supporting the outfit’s youth-led protests, while extending solidarity with the INDIA bloc rally on the “vote chori” charge. He, however, said that the CJP would retain its independent identity and not join the Sunday protest by the opposition parties. Mr. Dipke said he had called on Ms. Banerjee to express gratitude for her support to the outfit’s first protest at Jantar Mantar on the NEET paper leak issue and her backing when its leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were arrested by the Delhi Police. Left leaders on Saturday (October 31) accused Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar of undermining universal adult franchise through the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise, with CPI(M) MP John Brittas alleging that even elected representatives are being made to establish their eligibility to vote. The CEC has lost the moral and legal authority to remain in office, he asserted. Speaking at the INDIA bloc’s “public impeachment” programme, Mr. Brittas said citizens who had exercised their franchise for decades are now finding their names deleted from electoral rolls, being summoned for hearings, and being told to prove their existence. The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Saturday (October 31, 2026) accused the Congress and its allies of ridiculing democratic institutions by staging a mock Parliament session, and said that Opposition parties had repeatedly disrupted proceedings in the real Parliament. At a press conference, BJP MP Sambit Patra referred to the structure resembling the old Parliament building erected for the mock Parliament session and said: “They want to retain everything from the old British-era structure... They should seat Rahul Gandhi ji as the mock Prime Minister in that very old structure. We have absolutely no objection.” BJP ridicules INDIA bloc’s mock Parliament, defends SIR, political double standards, and highlights alleged vote protection amid poverty claims. The chair on which former Lok Sabha Speaker Meira Kumar sat while presiding over the INDIA bloc’s “public impeachment” of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar on Saturday (October 31) was once occupied by the country’s first Prime Minister, Jawaharlal Nehru. The information was provided by Congress’ media and publicity department head Pawan Khera, who was involved with organising the symbolic public impeachment. Today, in that very chair, invoking the spirit of Nehru, former Lok Sabha Speaker Meira Kumar pronounced Gyanesh Kumar unfit to continue as the Chief Election Commissioner of India, Mr. Khera said. The Janata Dal (United) on Saturday (OCtober 31) termed the INDIA bloc’s public impeachment exercise against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar a “drama”, accusing the Congress of trying to push the country towards anarchy. JD(U) national spokesperson Rajeev Ranjan Prasad told PTI that the exercise does not reflect the role of a constructive opposition and that the entire episode reflects an extremist perspective and will not help resolve any dispute. “This is not going to resolve any dispute in any manner. It is an attempt to push the country towards anarchy,” Mr. Prasad told PTI . The Indian National Developmental, Inclusive Alliance’s symbolic “public impeachment” of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar on Saturday (October 31, 2026) featured accounts from voters who alleged that their names had been deleted from electoral rolls during the special intensive revision (SIR) exercise. Among them was Anita Jaiswal, who moved from Kolkata to Delhi. She said she had voted in every election between 2012 and 2025 but was now being asked to establish her citizenship. Voters allege name removals in SIR; activists condemn EC during CEC Gyanesh Kumar impeachment at Kharge residence, New Delhi. Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Saturday (October 31) demanded the immediate removal of CEC Gyanesh Kumar and the scrapping of the 2023 law providing immunity to the CEC, accusing the poll panel chief of working under the directions of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah. “The Modi government has hatched every conspiracy since 2014 to cling to power: stealing MPs, breaking parties, stealing governments, electoral bonds, misuse of ED/CBI. And now vote theft -- cut opposition votes and rule,” he alleged, adding that there are hundreds of examples of “vote chori”. The Indian National Developmental Inclusive Alliance (INDIA) on Saturday (October 31, 2026) carried out a symbolic “public impeachment” of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, unanimously adopting a motion by a show of hands. They levelled six charges against him, including conspiring with the ruling BJP to steal elections, deleting 13.2 crore voters through the special intensive revision (SIR) of voter lists, and acting at the behest of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah. INDIA bloc stages symbolic public impeachment of CEC Gyanesh Kumar on six charges, claiming electoral manipulation and threats to voters, prompting warnings to officials. 截取自YouTube的屏幕录像显示，2026年11月1日，新德里拉姆利拉广场正在为印度全国发展赢得包容联盟（INDIA）针对首席选举专员贾内什·库马尔的集会做准备。

印度全国发展赢得包容联盟（INDIA）计划于11月1日星期日在德里的拉姆利拉广场举行大型集会。反对党领导人及来自不同邦的支持者正陆续抵达首都，以展示力量，反对据称存在的选举违规行为，并要求首席选举专员贾内什·库马辞职。

10月31日星期六，该联盟通过举手表决一致通过一项决议，对首席选举专员贾内什·库马举行象征性的“公开弹劾”。联盟提出了六项指控，包括与执政的印度人民党（BJP）串通窃取选举、通过选民名册特别集中修订（SIR）删除1320万名选民，以及听命于总理纳伦德拉·莫迪和内政部长阿米特·沙阿行事。

西孟加拉邦的反对党加大了针对该邦特别集中修订后提交的161万份选民纳入上诉案件的施压力度。印度全国国大党（TMC）和印度共产党（马克思主义）领导人质疑，在该邦完成特别集中修订后，究竟是谁授权提交这些上诉。

西孟加拉邦反对党就161万份选民纳入上诉询问选举委员会，并因问责问题及特别集中修订争议向其施压。

联邦部长哈迪普·辛格·普里星期六表示，INDIA联盟即将在德里举行的集会是“严重的政治错误”，并要求国大党领导人拉胡尔·甘地“反省”。普里称，INDIA联盟原定11月1日星期日举行的集会“对42年前发生的大规模暴行完全漠不关心”。他指出，鉴于节庆季到来，商界也敦促国大党重新考虑集会日期。

蟑螂人民党（CJP）创始人阿布希吉特·迪普克于10月31日星期六在德里会见了国大党（TMC）最高领导人马马塔·班纳吉，感谢她支持该党由青年主导的抗议活动，同时声援INDIA联盟针对“窃取选票”指控举行的集会。不过，他表示，CJP将保持独立身份，不参加反对党于星期日举行的抗议活动。

迪普克称，他曾拜访班纳吉女士，感谢她支持该党于中央广场就全国普通中学教育证书考试（NEET）试题泄露事件举行的首次抗议，并在该党领导人绍拉夫·达斯和阿舒托什·兰卡被德里警方逮捕时为她提供支持。

左翼领导人于10月31日星期六指控首席选举专员贾内什·库马通过特别集中修订活动破坏普选权。印度共产党（马克思主义）议员约翰·布里塔斯称，就连当选代表也被要求证明其投票资格。他断言，首席选举专员已经失去继续任职的道德和法律权威。

布里塔斯在INDIA联盟的“公开弹劾”活动中表示，数十年间一直行使选举权的公民如今发现自己的姓名被从选民名册中删除，还被要求参加聆讯并证明自己仍然存在。

印度人民党（BJP）于10月31日星期六（2026年）指责国大党及其盟友通过仿造议会会议嘲弄民主制度，并称反对党曾多次扰乱真正议会的议事进程。在一次新闻发布会上，BJP议员桑比特·帕特拉提到为仿造议会会议搭建的、仿照旧议会大楼的建筑，并表示：“他们想保留英国统治时期那座旧建筑的一切……他们完全可以让拉胡尔·甘地先生坐上那座老建筑里的模拟总理席位。我们绝对没有异议。”

BJP嘲笑INDIA联盟的模拟议会，为特别集中修订辩护，批评其政治双重标准，并强调有人声称在有关贫困的争议中保护选票。

前人民院议长梅拉·库马尔于10月31日星期六主持INDIA联盟对首席选举专员贾内什·库马尔的“公开弹劾”时所坐的椅子，曾由该国首任总理贾瓦哈拉尔·尼赫鲁坐过。参与组织这场象征性公开弹劾活动的国大党媒体与宣传部门负责人帕万·凯拉提供了相关信息。凯拉说，梅拉·库马尔当天坐在那把椅子上，以尼赫鲁的精神宣布贾内什·库马不再适合担任印度首席选举专员。

人民党（联合）于10月31日星期六称INDIA联盟针对首席选举专员贾内什·库马举行的公开弹劾活动是一场“闹剧”，并指责国大党试图把国家推向无政府状态。JD(U)全国发言人拉杰夫·兰詹·普拉萨德告诉印度斯坦新闻通讯社（PTI），这项活动并未体现建设性反对派应有的作用，整个事件反映出极端主义思维，无助于解决任何争端。

普拉萨德对PTI表示：“这无论如何都无法解决任何争端。这是在试图把国家推向无政府状态。”

印度全国发展赢得包容联盟于10月31日星期六（2026年）对首席选举专员贾内什·库马举行象征性的“公开弹劾”，通过举手表决一致通过一项决议。联盟提出了六项指控，包括与执政的印度人民党（BJP）串通窃取选举、通过选民名册特别集中修订（SIR）删除1320万名选民，以及听命于总理纳伦德拉·莫迪和内政部长阿米特·沙阿行事。

INDIA联盟就六项指控对首席选举专员贾内什·库马举行象征性公开弹劾，称其操纵选举并威胁选民，引发对有关官员的警告。

11月1日星期日，INDIA联盟计划在德里的拉姆利拉广场举行大型集会。反对党领导人及来自不同邦的支持者正陆续抵达首都，以展示力量，反对据称存在的选举违规行为，并要求首席选举专员贾内什·库马辞职。

此次动员并不限于联盟内的政治组成部分。

https://leadership.ng/plateau-imo-cross-.body: Many public primary and secondary schools across the country are grappling with an acute shortage of teachers, a development that threatens effective teaching and learning, particularly in rural communities. Findings by LEADERSHIP Sunday have revealed that teacher retirements without replacement, poor welfare and remuneration, rural-urban migration and unwillingness to accept postings to remote communities are among the major factors worsening the crisis. LEADERSHIP Sunday investigations across Cross River, Delta, Ondo, Imo, Plateau and Oyo states showed varying degrees of teacher shortages, with Plateau, Imo and Cross River emerging as some of the worst-affected states. While some schools operate with only a handful of teachers handling multiple subjects, others struggle to provide qualified teachers for critical subjects, leaving pupils and students at a disadvantage. In Cross River State, about 11,861 teachers are teaching from Primary One to Six across the three senatorial districts. The director of Administration (DA), State Universal Basic Education Board (SUBEB), Mr Joseph Effiom, who spoke on behalf of the chairman, Chief Margaret Fidelia Okpo Ene, disclosed this in an interaction with LEADERSHIP Sunday in Calabar. Effiom said the board could not provide the figure for Junior Secondary School teachers from JSS 1 to 3 because the authority for junior secondary education had yet to be formally transferred from the Ministry of Education to SUBEB. He said SUBEB was in dire need of over 2,000 teachers, as well as 500 security personnel to protect infrastructure across schools in the state’s 18 local government areas. “SUBEB is in dire need of 2,000 more teachers with 500 security men to safeguard basic infrastructure across schools in the state,” Effiom said. Findings by LEADERSHIP Sunday revealed that while the state Ministry of Education puts the number of secondary school teachers at about 6,400 for over 280 public secondary schools, many rural schools have only three to five teachers handling all subjects. A teacher in one of the schools in Calabar, who preferred not to be named in print, expressed dismay, lamenting that having one teacher handle four subjects was unhealthy for educational development. He decried the absence of Mathematics teachers in a school in his hometown in the Cross River Central Senatorial District, where he hails from. A retired headmaster in Cross River State, Mr Abang (surname withheld), said one of the reasons behind the shortage of teachers was retirement without replacement, noting that over 3,000 teachers retired between 2018 and 2024 without replacement due to an embargo on employment. LEADERSHIP Sunday gathered that other factors responsible for the shortage include rural-urban migration, as teachers posted to rural areas lobby their way back to urban centres such as Calabar, Ogoja and Ikom, leaving schools in the hinterlands understaffed. The Cross River State Chairman of the Nigeria Union of Teachers (NUT), Comrade Gregory Olayi, described the teacher shortage as alarming, calling on governments at all levels not to turn a deaf ear to the problem. On his part, the Nigeria Union of Teachers (NUT) in Delta State has lamented the acute shortage of teachers and instructional materials required for effective teaching and learning in primary and secondary schools across the state. The NUT chairman in the state, Comrade Dickson Poubeni, called on Governor Sheriff Oborevwori to put the necessary machinery in place to address the challenge and ensure a peaceful and conducive teaching and learning environment in schools. He said there was a recent approval for salary grade level 17 progression for university graduate teachers in the primary school system. The commissioner for Technical Education, Hon. Smart Ufoh, said while the work of teachers might not always attract public attention, its impact was reflected in the lives and achievements of their students. He said the state government had plans to fill vacancies in schools, especially in remote areas and in critical subject areas. On the challenges of teacher recruitment, some teachers alleged that payments were being demanded for preferred postings after appointments. A teacher recently transferred from Ekredjebor, Ughelli North LGA, alleged that, “The whole system is rotten. They collect money and transfer people to wherever they want. The choice depends on what you pay. I was transferred and paid N50,000 before I was transferred back to where I wanted after two weeks.” A principal, Patricia, alleged that her inability to pay influenced her posting. “Transfer is to the highest bidder, because I am a widow and don’t have the funds. I was taken to a school in a remote village without WAEC accreditation and less than 200 students,” she said. Another teacher, Victoria, said: “I didn’t pay the N50,000 transfer fee, so I was transferred to a riverine school in Ewu. This has been the trend over the years, it is sad.” Similarly, students in some public schools in Ondo State are struggling to learn due to a shortage of teachers, with some secondary school students preparing for the West African Senior School Certificate Examination (WASSCE) reportedly without teachers for key subjects. The situation has raised concerns among students and teachers over its impact on academic performance, classroom learning and the workload of available teachers. A student, Francis, from a school in Ido-Ani, a rural community in Ose Local Government Area, said the number of teachers available in his school fluctuated, affecting students’ interest in attending classes. “In our own school, I don’t even know the number of teachers we have. At times, we will see four teachers in the whole school; other times, we will see two teachers. This has really affected us because most times, we are not even interested in going to school because there is no teacher available to teach us,” he said. A teacher, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said the shortage had increased the workload of those still in service, with some handling multiple subjects across several classrooms. “Imagine a single teacher teaching two to three subjects in more than six classrooms, with each class having more than 100 students. The time we feel the stress the most is during examinations. Marking scripts is very stressful, and at the end of everything, we most times fall sick,” the teacher said, calling on the government to address the situation. Reacting to the crisis, the Ondo State Commissioner for Education, Igbekele Ajibefun, attributed the shortage partly to years of inadequate recruitment, during which teachers retired without being replaced. Ajibefun said the state recruited more than 2,000 teachers in 2025, adding that the exercise had improved staffing levels but had not completely bridged the gap. “Though not all schools have the required number of teachers now, I want to assure you that soon, more teachers will be recruited to continue to fill the gap,” he said. The commissioner said the number of teachers required to fill the gap could not be determined precisely because retirements continued to change the staffing situation. He disclosed that more than 100 teachers could retire in a month. He added that the government’s recruitment target was to bring more teachers into the system than the number leaving through retirement. Ajibefun also acknowledged that low salaries discouraged young people from entering the teaching profession, arguing that better remuneration was needed to attract and retain teachers. The chairman of the Ondo State Teaching Service Commission (TESCOM), Dr Oluwadayisi Oke, also acknowledged the shortage, saying the government was making efforts to improve teachers’ welfare through training, retraining and the regular payment of salaries and pensions. Oke expressed optimism that improved welfare would encourage more young people to take up teaching, while indicating that further recruitment was expected. Meanwhile, the shortage has prompted some school alumni associations to intervene. The Vice-President of Imade College Owo Old Students Association (IMACOSA), Surveyor Felix Ajibade, said the association had employed 29 ad hoc teachers to support teaching at the school. Ajibade said the association paid each teacher N70,000 monthly to prevent students from suffering the consequences of inadequate staffing. He appealed to the government to provide more teachers to public schools. Findings by LEADERSHIP Sunday showed that Ondo State has 6,880 teachers in public primary schools, according to records obtained from the State Universal Basic Education Board (SUBEB). However, the number of teachers serving in public secondary schools and the estimated number of additional teachers required to address staffing gaps across primary and secondary schools could not be established. Efforts to obtain comments from the state chairman of the Nigeria Union of Teachers (NUT), Leke Alebiosu, were unsuccessful, as he did not respond to repeated calls and messages. The Imo State commissioner for Education, Ben Ikeguruka, disclosed that, according to the ministry’s records, the state had 6,641 teachers serving in public primary and secondary schools. He said the ministry’s needs assessment revealed that the state required an additional 12,000 teachers to fill the existing gap. However, available indications suggest that teachers are grossly inadequate, a situation confirmed by both the ministry’s and NUT’s records. Feelers revealed that Governor Hope Uzodimma had yet to recruit any teachers but was making moves to employ more teachers. The challenges confronting primary and secondary education in the state include rural-urban imbalance, poor welfare and inadequate remuneration. Teachers are also known to reject postings to remote, riverine and hard-to-reach areas. This attitude is largely attributed to the absence of rural allowances and accommodation, as well as poor salary structures. The Imo State NUT chairman, Comrade Akujobi Nwokoro, said the union had been engaging with the state government on the need to recruit more teachers into the system. “What we have for now is not enough to go round,” he said, calling on the government to do the needful. Similarly, the Plateau State chairman of the Nigeria Union of Teachers (NUT), Mr Kefas Nanpan, decried the severe shortage of teachers across public schools in the state. He hinted that the number of public school teachers in Plateau State had plummeted from about 24,000 in 2013 to fewer than 13,000 in 2026. According to him, the acute shortage had left numerous public and rural schools operating with just a headmaster and a single classroom teacher, or sometimes only one or two teachers for an entire school. Meanwhile, officials of the Plateau State Ministry of Education and SUBEB declined to disclose the number of primary and secondary school teachers currently on the government’s payroll. However, a retired teacher from Tudun Wada in Jos North LGA, Bulus Choji, told our correspondent that teachers in primary and secondary schools in the state were grossly inadequate. According to him, teachers were retiring without replacement, adding that brain drain, poor recruitment exercises over the last five to 10 years, refusal to accept postings to rural areas and insecurity in some LGAs had contributed to the shortage of teachers in the state. The staff strength in Oyo State’s public secondary schools is 26,436, managed through the Post-Primary Schools Teaching Service Commission (TESCOM), up from 13,730 in 2019. This followed recruitment drives, including the recent employment of 7,500 teaching and 3,000 non-teaching staff.
https://leadership.ng/plateau-imo-cross-.title_zh: 教师短缺持续，伊莫州高原、克罗斯里弗州公立学校受影响最严重
https://leadership.ng/plateau-imo-cross-.body_zh: 全国各地许多公立小学和中学正面临教师严重短缺，这一情况威胁有效教学和学习，乡村社区尤其严重。《领导力星期日》的调查结果显示，教师退休后无人接替、福利和薪酬较差、乡村人口向城市迁移，以及不愿接受偏远社区的派任，是加剧这一危机的主要因素。《领导力星期日》对夸比河州、三角洲州、翁多州、伊莫州、普拉托州和奥约州的调查显示，各地教师短缺程度不一，其中普拉托州、伊莫州和夸比河州是受影响最严重的州之一。有些学校只有少数几名教师，却要教授多门科目；另一些学校则难以为核心科目配备合格教师，使学生处于不利地位。在夸比河州，约有11,861名教师分布在三个选区的学校，教授小学一年级至六年级课程。州基础教育委员会（SUBEB）行政主任约瑟夫·埃菲奥姆先生代表主席玛格丽特·菲德莉亚·奥克波·埃内女士接受《领导力星期日》采访时，在卡拉巴尔披露了上述情况。埃菲奥姆说，由于初中教育事务尚未从教育部正式移交给州基础教育委员会（SUBEB），该委员会无法提供初中一年级至三年级的教师人数。他说，州基础教育委员会急需新增2,000多名教师，还需要500名安保人员，以保护全州18个地方政府辖区各学校的基础设施。埃菲奥姆说：“州基础教育委员会急需2,000名教师和500名安保人员，以保护全州各学校的基础设施。”《领导力星期日》的调查显示，州教育部称280多所公立中学约有6,400名中学教师，但许多乡村学校只有三至五名教师，需要教授所有科目。卡拉巴尔一所学校的一名教师不愿具名，对一名教师教授四门科目的状况表示震惊，认为这不利于教育发展。他对家乡夸比河中央选区一所学校缺少数学教师表示遗憾。夸比河州一名退休校长阿邦先生（未透露姓氏）说，教师短缺的原因之一是退休后无人接替；由于招聘受到限制，2018年至2024年间有3,000多名教师退休后未获补员。《领导者星期日》获悉，造成教师短缺的其他因素包括乡村人口向城市迁移。被派往乡村地区的教师会设法回到卡拉巴尔、奥戈贾和伊科姆等城市中心工作，导致边远地区学校人员不足。尼日利亚教师工会（Nut）夸比河州主席格雷戈里·奥拉伊同志称，教师短缺情况令人担忧，呼吁各级政府不要对这一问题置若罔闻。尼日利亚教师工会（Nut）三角洲州分会则对全州小学和中学有效教学与学习所急需的教师及教学材料严重短缺表示遗憾。该州工会主席迪克森·普贝尼同志呼吁州长谢里夫·奥博雷沃里采取必要措施应对这一挑战，确保学校拥有和平、有利于教学和学习的环境。他说，最近已批准小学系统中大学学历教师晋升至薪级17级。技术教育专员斯马特·乌福夫阁下说，教师的工作虽然未必总能吸引公众关注，但其影响体现在学生的生活和成就中。他说，州政府计划填补学校空缺，尤其是偏远地区和核心科目领域的空缺。在教师招聘面临的问题上，一些教师称，获聘后如想获得理想派任，便需支付费用。一名最近从乌盖利北地方政府辖区埃克雷杰博尔调动的教师称：“整个体系已经腐败。他们收钱，然后把人调到他们想去的地方。去哪里取决于你付多少钱。我被调走前付了N50,000，两周后又被调回自己想去的岗位。”一名校长帕特里夏称，她无力支付相关费用，因此影响了她的派任。她说：“调任由出价最高者决定，因为我是寡妇，没有资金。我被派到偏远村庄的一所学校，那所学校没有西非国家考试委员会（WAEC）认证，学生不到200人。”另一名教师维多利亚说：“我没有支付N50,000的调任费，所以被派到埃武的一所沿河学校。多年来一直是这样，令人悲伤。”同样，翁多州一些公立学校的学生也因教师短缺而难以学习。据报道，一些中学生在准备西非高级中学证书考试（WASSCE）时，关键科目没有教师授课。这一状况引发学生和教师对学业成绩、课堂教学及在职教师工作负担所受影响的担忧。奥塞地方政府辖区乡村社区伊多阿尼一所学校的学生弗朗西斯说，学校可支配的教师人数不断波动，影响学生到课学习的兴趣。他说：“在我们学校，我甚至不知道我们有多少教师。有时全校只能看到四名教师，有时只能看到两名教师。这确实影响了我们，因为多数时候我们都不想去上学，因为没有教师教我们。”一名要求匿名的教师说，教师短缺增加了仍在岗教师的工作负担，有些人需要在多个班级教授多门科目。这名教师说：“想象一下，一名教师要在六个以上的教室教授两至三门科目，每个班都有100多名学生。考试期间是我们压力最大的时候。阅卷非常累人，而最终我们很多时候都会病倒。”他呼吁政府处理这一问题。针对这场危机，翁多州教育专员伊格贝凯勒·阿吉贝丰将短缺部分归因于多年来招聘不足，在此期间教师退休后无人补替。阿吉贝丰说，该州于2025年招聘了2,000多名教师，此举改善了人员配置，但尚未完全弥合缺口。他说：“尽管目前并非所有学校都有足够数量的教师，但我想向你们保证，很快将招聘更多教师，继续填补缺口。”这位专员说，由于退休人数持续变化，无法精确确定填补缺口所需的教师人数。他透露，一个月内可能有100多名教师退休。他补充说，政府招聘的目标是让入职教师人数超过退休人数。阿吉贝丰还承认，薪资较低使年轻人不愿从事教师工作，认为需要提高薪酬以吸引和留住教师。翁多州教师服务委员会（TESCOM）主席奥卢瓦达伊西·奥克博士也承认存在教师短缺，并表示政府正通过培训、再培训以及按时发放工资和养老金，努力改善教师福利。奥克乐观地表示，福利改善将鼓励更多年轻人从事教学，同时透露预计还会继续招聘。与此同时，教师短缺促使一些校友会采取行动介入。伊马德学院奥沃校友会（IMACOSA）副主席、测量师费利克斯·阿吉巴德说，校友会聘用了29名临时教师协助学校教学。阿吉巴德说，校友会每月向每名教师支付N70,000，以免学生因人员配备不足而受到影响。他呼吁政府向公立学校提供更多教师。《领导力星期日》的调查显示，根据从州基础教育委员会（SUBEB）获得的记录，翁多州公立小学有6,880名教师。然而，公立中学在岗教师人数，以及为解决小学和中学人员配置缺口而估算所需的新增教师人数，均无法确定。记者多次致电和发送信息，试图向尼日利亚教师工会（Nut）翁多州主席莱克·阿列比奥苏征求意见，但未获回应。伊莫州教育专员本·伊克古鲁卡披露，根据该部记录，全州公立小学和中学共有6,641名教师。他说，该部需求评估显示，需要新增12,000名教师才能填补现有缺口。然而，现有迹象表明教师数量严重不足，该部及尼日利亚教师工会（Nut）的记录均证实了这一点。消息人士透露，州长霍普·乌佐迪马尚未招聘任何教师，但正在采取行动雇用更多教师。该州小学和中学面临的挑战包括城乡失衡、福利欠佳和薪酬不足。教师也经常拒绝派往偏远、沿河和难以抵达的地区。这种态度主要被归因于缺少乡村补贴和住房，以及薪资结构不合理。伊莫州尼日利亚教师工会（Nut）主席阿库乔比·恩沃科罗同志说，工会一直与州政府交涉，要求招聘更多教师进入该教育系统。他说：“我们目前拥有的人手根本不够分配。”他呼吁政府采取必要措施。同样，普拉托州尼日利亚教师工会（Nut）主席凯法斯·南潘先生也对全州公立学校教师严重短缺表示遗憾。他暗示，普拉托州公立学校教师人数已从2013年的约24,000人骤降至2026年的不足13,000人。据他称，严重短缺导致许多公立和乡村学校只有一名校长和一名课堂教师，有时整所学校也只有一两名教师。与此同时，普拉托州教育部和州基础教育委员会（SUBEB）官员拒绝披露目前由政府支付薪酬的公立学校教师人数。然而，乔斯北地方政府辖区图登瓦达的一名退休教师布卢斯·乔吉告诉记者，该州中小学教师数量严重不足。他说，教师退休后无人接替；此外，人才流失、过去五至10年招聘工作不力、教师拒绝接受乡村地区派任，以及部分地方政府辖区安全局势不佳，也促成了该州教师短缺。奥约州公立中学在岗教师为26,436人，由中学教师服务委员会（TESCOM）管理，较2019年的13,730人有所增加。这得益于多轮招聘，包括近期聘用的7,500名教学人员和3,000名非教学人员。

https://www.myjoyonline.com/crypto-firm-.summary_zh: 全球最大的加密货币交易所币安表示，已赔付周四黑客攻击中被窃取的63亿美元（47亿英镑）资产中的90%。币安一直承诺全额赔付这场疑似有记录以来规模最大的加密货币黑客攻击造成的损失，并称已预留超过63.4亿美元的公司资金用于赔付。
https://www.myjoyonline.com/crypto-firm-.body: Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, says it has covered 90% of the $6.3bn (£4.7bn) assets stolen in a hack on Thursday. The remaining 10% may take longer to source in the required amounts, the company added. Binance has consistently pledged to cover 100% of the losses from what is suspected to be crypto's biggest hack on record and said it has set aside more than $6.34bn in company funds to do so. "Binance will absorb the financial impact of these stolen funds, not our users," the company said in a statement on Saturday. The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) said on Saturday that North Korea was responsible for the hack. Two analytics firms previously told the BBC they had robust intelligence pointing to North Korean state-backed hacking unit the Lazarus Group, also known as TraderTraitor - which was specifically named by the FBI - as the likely culprits. Binance said it had replenished the stolen assets using various funds and its own corporate treasury. All holdings of the cryptocurrencies bitcoin, ethereum and Tether are covered, along with seven other widely-traded crypto assets, the company said. The company said its next goal is resuming withdrawal services for users, saying it remained on track to reopen withdrawals on Sunday 1 November and would provide a further update once details were confirmed. The hack is believed to be the largest in history, eclipsing the record of a $1.5bn heist on the Bybit exchange in 2025 - for which the FBI also said North Korea was responsible. Binance's initial investigation suggested an engineer's laptop was compromised, which allowed access to unauthorised withdrawals, but a later update said they had uncovered "additional points of breach". Richard Teng, Binance's co-chief executive officer, said the hack was carried out by more than one person, and the hackers used sophisticated methods to hide their tracks, such as a "self-destruct mechanism". On Friday, the company said it had frozen around $3bn of stolen assets after working with law enforcement, intelligence firms and partners. The investigation is ongoing, it added. The US Secret Service said on Friday it is "working around the clock" with private sector partners "to identify, freeze, trace, and recover funds" stolen from Binance. Binance, founded in China in 2017, lets users buy, sell and trade digital assets - it is estimated to have hundreds of millions of users worldwide. Crypto is a digital asset, which doesn't exist physically and is instead accessed via digital wallets or computers
https://www.myjoyonline.com/crypto-firm-.title_zh: 加密货币公司Binance承担黑客攻击造成的90%损失，金额达63亿美元
https://www.myjoyonline.com/crypto-firm-.body_zh: 全球最大的加密货币交易所 Binance 表示，针对周四发生的一次黑客攻击，公司已赔付被盗的 63亿美元（47亿英镑）资产中的90%。公司补充称，追回剩余10%所需的相应数额可能需要更长时间。Binance 一直承诺承担这起疑似加密货币史上最大黑客事件造成的全部损失，并表示已预留超过63.4亿美元的公司资金用于赔付。公司周六发表声明称：“被盗资金造成的财务影响将由 Binance 承担，而不是由我们的用户承担。”美国联邦调查局（FBI）周六表示，朝鲜对此次黑客攻击负责。此前，两家分析机构曾告诉 BBC，它们掌握可靠情报，指向朝鲜国家支持的黑客组织 Lazarus Group（又称 TraderTraitor）——FBI 也特别点名了该组织——认为其是此次事件的罪魁祸首。Binance 表示，已动用多种资金及自有公司资金补足被盗资产。公司称，Bitcoin、Ethereum 和 Tether 加密货币的所有持仓均在赔付范围内，另外还涵盖 7 种交易量较大的加密资产。公司表示，下一目标是恢复用户提币服务，并称仍有望在 11 月 1 日星期日重新开放提币，待细节确认后将提供进一步更新。此次黑客事件被认为是史上规模最大的一起，超过了 2025 年 Bybit 交易所 15亿美元被盗案的纪录；FBI 对该案也称朝鲜负有责任。Binance 的初步调查表明，一台工程师的笔记本电脑遭到入侵，导致未经授权的提币操作得以进行；但公司随后更新称，已发现“其他入侵突破口”。Binance 联席首席执行官 Richard Teng 表示，此次攻击由多人实施，黑客还采用精密手法隐藏行踪，例如设置“自毁机制”。公司周五表示，在与执法机构、情报机构及合作伙伴协作后，已冻结约30亿美元被盗资产。调查仍在进行中。美国特勤局周五表示，正与私营部门合作伙伴“昼夜不停开展工作”，以“识别、冻结、追踪并追回”从 Binance 盗走的资金。Binance 于 2017 年在中国成立，允许用户买卖和交易数字资产，据估计全球用户数达数亿。加密货币是一种并不实体存在、而是通过数字钱包或电脑访问的数字资产

https://www.yna.co.kr/view/akr2026110103.title: 태국 인권변호사, 왕실모독 혐의로 추가 징역형…총 38년 수감

https://www.yna.co.kr/view/akr2026110103.body_zh: （雅加达＝韩联社）曾于6年前在泰国呼吁王室改革并主导反政府示威的知名人权律师，最近又因王室不敬罪被追加判处有期徒刑，累计服刑时间将达到38年。据EFE、法新社及泰国媒体《曼谷邮报》等1日（当地时间）报道，泰国法院近日以王室不敬罪对被起诉的人权律师阿农·南帕（41岁）判处有期徒刑2年8个月。阿农此前已因同一罪名多次被判刑，并自2023年起服刑；此次判决后，他因王室不敬罪累计获判的刑期增至38年。韩国5·18纪念财团承认阿农曾作为泰国民主化运动的主力开展活动，并选定其为次年光州人权奖获奖者。判决庭审结束后，阿农的律师向法新社表示：“王室不敬罪已经沦为压制反对势力的政治工具。”泰国刑法第112条规定的王室不敬罪规定，侮辱或负面描绘国王、王后、王储等王室成员及王室的功绩者，最高可判处15年监禁。据泰国人权律师协会称，自2020年11月以来，包括未成年人在内，共有285人因涉嫌王室不敬罪被起诉。2020年，泰国反政府示威在野党未来前进党（FFP）于同年2月获得年轻人广泛支持、随后因宪法法院裁决被强制解散后，以大学城为中心开始。示威一度因新冠疫情扩散而中止，同年7月中旬恢复后，不仅要求改革君主制，还提出了总理辞职和修宪等诉求。报道：KakaoTalk okjebo〈版权所有(c) 韩联社，未经许可禁止转载、再发布及用于人工智能学习和应用〉2026/11/01 17:17发稿，2026年11月01日17时17分发稿

Unlock these with Subscription Security personnel are making efforts to rescue six Indian tourists, including two women, stranded due to heavy snowfall in the Shey-Phoksundo National Park area of Nepal since Saturday afternoon (October 31, 2026), officials said on Sunday (November 1, 2026). The tourists had gone to the Dho area in Shey Phoksundo Rural Municipality’s Ward No. 8, which was covered in heavy snow, according to Dolpa Chief District Officer Junu Dhakal. Shey Phoksundo Lake, located in the rural municipality, is Nepal’s deepest lake. It is situated at an altitude of 3,600 metres and has an estimated depth of 145 metres. “We have located the area where they are stranded, and an Army helicopter is arriving to rescue them. We hope to rescue them soon,” Ms. Dhakal told PTI . The Indian tourists had ventured into the area despite warnings from security personnel and the Nepali guide accompanying them, she said. Ms. Dhakal said the tourists left the guide and proceeded towards the lake area despite heavy snowfall. Communication with them was disrupted on Saturday night (October 31, 2026). The guide contacted the District Administration Office in Dolpa on Saturday evening (October 31, 2026), saying the tourists might have been stranded due to heavy snowfall, she said. However, communication was completely disrupted on Sunday morning (November 1, 2026). “We cannot say they are missing, as we have located the area,” Ms. Dhakal clarified. The tourists have been identified as Moumita Halder, Piyali Koley, Jajla Trivedi Kumar, Aditya Singha, Diplina Bishwas and Rajesh De, according to a press release issued by the District Administration Office, Dolpa. 尼泊尔官员周日（2026年11月1日）表示，自周六下午（2026年10月31日）以来，安全人员一直设法营救6名因大雪受困于尼泊尔谢伊—福克松多国家公园地区的印度游客，其中包括2名女性。

据多尔帕首席区行政官朱努·达卡尔介绍，这些游客曾前往谢伊福克松多农村市镇第8区的多地区，那里被大雪覆盖。位于该农村市镇的谢伊福克松多湖是尼泊尔最深的湖泊，海拔3,600米，估计水深145米。

达卡尔女士告诉印度 PTI ：“我们已经确定了他们受困的位置，一架军用直升机正在赶来营救他们。我们希望很快就能把他们救出。”

她说，尽管安全人员和随行尼泊尔向导发出了警告，这些印度游客仍进入了该地区。达卡尔女士表示，尽管大雪纷飞，游客们还是离开向导，前往湖区。周六夜间（2026年10月31日），与他们的通信中断。

她说，周六傍晚（2026年10月31日），向导联系了多尔帕地区行政办公室，称游客可能因大雪而受困。然而，周日上午（2026年11月1日），通信完全中断。

达卡尔女士澄清说：“我们不能说他们失踪了，因为我们已经确定了他们所在的位置。”

据多尔帕地区行政办公室发布的新闻稿，这6名游客分别是莫米塔·哈尔德、皮亚利·科利、贾杰拉·特里维迪·库马尔、阿迪蒂亚·辛哈、迪普莉娜·比什瓦斯和拉杰什·德。

新闻稿称，安全人员正在动员，救援直升机预计很快抵达。

https://www.premiumtimesng.com/opinion/9.summary: In Nigeria, the largest Black population in the world, many students and youths are actually snoring as the struggle for the future of their country in the 2027 general elections gets underway. However, these do not mean that the barricades cannot go up in such countries. When the students and youths move, society changes.
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/opinion/9.summary_zh: 尼日利亚拥有世界上规模最大的黑人人口，许多学生和青年实际上正在酣睡，而这场围绕国家未来、在2027年大选中展开的角逐才刚拉开序幕。然而，这并不意味着这类国家无法筑起路障。当学生和青年行动起来时，社会就会改变。
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/opinion/9.body: The situation in France is similar to its 1968 Students Uprising, when the parents and grandparents of today’s protesters seized the country. Over 10 million people took to the streets, and the then French President Charles de Gaulle, on May 29, 1968, fled to Germany. When the famous war general returned, he dissolved the National Assembly and called new elections. The 1968 French student demands were for more classrooms to reduce university overcrowding, democracy in schools, educational reforms, and a world free from injustice, such as the United States’ genocide in Vietnam. Workers weighed in with strikes and factory occupations. They demanded higher salaries, better work conditions, and social reforms. Today, 58 years later, the demands are virtually the same, except that high school students have reduced the average age of the protesters. Unfazed by the deployment of over 70,000 police officers, they are protesting against teacher shortages, dilapidated school structures, cuts in school budgets, and inflation. By mid-October 2026, over 6,500 protesters, most of them minors, had been arrested. Over the October 17–18, 2026 weekend clashes alone, at least 2,500 arrests were made, while, in the October 24 protests, 1,435 persons were arrested. Even with the clashes and arrests in cities like Paris, Lyon, Bordeaux, and Marseille, the French government was in dialogue with the protesters, including reaching consensus on routes to take in order to minimize destruction of public property and offering concessions. However, as the French authorities try to reach understanding with the protesters, there are world leaders who want to divert attention and even escalate the crisis by urging them to clamp down on the protesters, whom they present as enemies. For instance, US President Donald Trump said the causes of the protests were not as stated by the protesters but were actually about immigration and integration. He wrote in his Truth Social post: “What’s happening in France is nothing less than out-of-control mass migration. This isn’t about schools; this is about Islam wanting to take over a once great country!” Trump told Americans: “Just look at France… Paris is going to be a Muslim city very soon.” He added: “France is burning! The immigration of people from an entirely different world, people with hatred in their hearts, has shattered that once great country.” He added: “Emmanuel (Macron) should have closed his borders a long time ago. I told him to do it.” Unstable Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu toed the Trump line, claiming France had “ceded to an invasion by Islamist extremists.” Equally, the Prime Ministers of Poland, Donald Tusk, and Hungary, Peter Magyar, sang the same hymn as Trump. However, the French leadership would not fall for such nonsense. Macron responded: “There has been a foreign manipulation of information since then, and that has led to some unacceptable and stupid comments from many foreign leaders.” Pointing out that some of the international postings on the protests were fake, he said: “We’ve seen AI images that show scenes that never happened in France. There are people who have stated that we were invaded by hordes of migrants and Islamists, which is completely false.” Macron’s rejection of false imputations is correct, although he does not go as far as admitting that the causes of the protests are mainly due to the economic crises the country is facing. Production has taken a downturn, with manufacturing, agriculture, and the broad industrial sectors contracting. By the second quarter of 2026, France’s public debt had reached €3.5955 trillion, or 119 percent of GDP. Its deficit is at 5.4 percent of GDP in 2026, in comparison to the European Union’s 3 percent limit. Since 2002, its debt has doubled as a share of GDP. Its pension deficits are projected to reach €15 billion by 2035. This is one of the grounds on which the trade unions joined the protests. France’s position has worsened in recent years with its increasing loss of the resources it has freely scooped for decades from its former African colonies. It lost its uranium and mining control in the Niger Republic. Its direct exploitation of countries like Burkina Faso, Mali, Guinea, and Senegal is being challenged, with even pliant Gabon giving notice of discontinuation. But France is not the only European country reeling under protests. In Albania, once a social haven, high school fees, corruption allegations, and rising mass unemployment sent the students into the streets. Clashes were recorded in Tirana and a number of cities. Protests rocked Italian cities like Milan, Turin, and Rome over high education costs and rising hardship. The protests in the Spanish cities of Madrid and Barcelona centred around high housing costs and pensions, while those in Portugal were on the cost of living and housing. In Europe generally, the student-worker alliances centre around a better education and work environment. But the country that has now taken the crown of student action is Serbia. There, rather than simply organize protests, the students decided to take over power by forming an opposition coalition against the ruling Serbian Progressive Party, SNS, which has been in power for the last fourteen years. They organized a non-partisan electoral list of professionals and social activists. In the October 25, 2026 parliamentary elections, the student coalition won 52.7 percent of the votes and 140 of 250 seats in the National Assembly. The ruling party secured 39.17 percent of the votes and 104 seats. Voter turnout was 68.78 percent. President Aleksandar Vucic conceded defeat. But while the European students are awake to their responsibilities, in many parts of the world, the students are sleeping. In Nigeria, the largest Black population in the world, many students and youths are actually snoring as the struggle for the future of their country in the 2027 general elections gets underway. More criminally, many of those who are awake are submitting themselves to be used as thugs and hired urchins by politicians whose antecedents are not secret. Apart from politicians and their children imposing leaders on students, there was a time when the president of the central National Association of Nigerian Students, NANS, was not even a student! However, these do not mean that the barricades cannot go up in such countries. When the students and youths move, society changes. Owei Lakemfa , a former secretary general of African workers, is a human rights activist, journalist and author

https://www.premiumtimesng.com/opinion/9.body_zh: 法国当前局势类似于1968年的学生起义，当时今天抗议者的父母和祖父母曾占领这个国家。超过1000万人走上街头，当时的法国总统戴高乐在1968年5月29日逃往德国。这位著名战争将军回国后，解散国民议会并宣布举行新的选举。1968年法国学生的要求是增加教室以缓解大学过度拥挤问题、在学校实行民主、进行教育改革，以及建立一个没有不公的世界，例如美国在越南进行的种族灭绝。工人们通过罢工和占领工厂加入进来。他们要求提高工资、改善工作条件并进行社会改革。今天，58年之后，这些要求几乎完全相同，只是高中生降低了抗议者的平均年龄。他们面对部署的超过7万名警察毫不畏惧，正在抗议教师短缺、校舍破败、学校预算削减以及通货膨胀。到2026年10月中旬，已有超过6500名抗议者被捕，其中大多数是未成年人。仅在2026年10月17日至18日的周末冲突中，就至少逮捕了2500人，而在10月24日的抗议活动中，有1435人被捕。即使在巴黎、里昂、波尔多和马赛等城市发生冲突和逮捕，法国政府仍与抗议者保持对话，包括就游行路线达成共识以尽量减少公共财产破坏，并作出让步。然而，在法国当局努力与抗议者达成谅解之际，一些世界领导人却想转移注意力，甚至通过敦促当局镇压抗议者来升级危机，他们将抗议者描述为敌人。例如，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普称抗议的原因并非抗议者所说的那样，而是关于移民和融合问题。他在Truth Social平台发帖写道：“法国正在发生的事情无非是失控的大规模移民。这与学校无关，这是伊斯兰想要接管一个曾经伟大的国家！”特朗普告诉美国人：“看看法国……巴黎很快就会成为一座穆斯林城市。”他补充说：“法国正在燃烧！来自完全不同世界的人的移民，那些心中充满仇恨的人，已经摧毁了那个曾经伟大的国家。”他还说：“埃马纽埃尔（马克龙）早就应该关闭边境。我告诉过他这么做。”立场不稳的以色列总理本雅明·内塔尼亚胡附和特朗普的说法，声称法国已经“向伊斯兰极端分子的入侵让步”。同样，波兰总理唐纳德·图斯克和匈牙利总理彼得·马贾尔也唱着与特朗普相同的调子。然而，法国领导层不会被这种无稽之谈所迷惑。马克龙回应道：“从那时起就出现了外国对信息的操纵，这导致许多外国领导人发表了一些不可接受且愚蠢的评论。”他指出一些关于抗议的国际帖文是伪造的，并说：“我们看到了人工智能生成的图像，显示了法国从未发生过的场景。有人声称我们被成群的移民和伊斯兰主义者入侵，这完全是虚假的。”马克龙拒绝虚假指责的做法是正确的，尽管他没有进一步承认抗议的主要原因是该国面临的经济危机。生产出现下滑，制造业、农业和广泛的工业部门都在收缩。到2026年第二季度，法国的公共债务已达到3.5955万亿欧元，占国内生产总值的119%。2026年其赤字占国内生产总值的5.4%，而欧盟的限制是3%。自2002年以来，其债务占国内生产总值的比例翻了一番。其养老金赤字预计到2035年将达到150亿欧元。这是工会加入抗议的理由之一。近年来，随着法国长期从其前非洲殖民地自由攫取的资源日益流失，其处境进一步恶化。它失去了在尼日尔共和国的铀和矿业控制权。它对布基纳法索、马里、几内亚和塞内加尔等国的直接剥削正受到挑战，甚至顺从的加蓬也发出终止通知。但法国并不是唯一陷入抗议困境的欧洲国家。在曾经是社会避风港的阿尔巴尼亚，高昂的学费、腐败指控和不断上升的大规模失业促使学生走上街头。在地拉那和一些城市发生了冲突。意大利的米兰、都灵和罗马等城市也因高昂的教育成本和日益严重的困难而爆发抗议。西班牙马德里和巴塞罗那城市的抗议集中在高房价和养老金问题上，而葡萄牙的抗议则针对生活成本和住房问题。在整个欧洲，学生与工人的联盟都围绕更好的教育和工作环境展开。但现在夺得学生行动桂冠的国家是塞尔维亚。在那里，学生们没有仅仅组织抗议，而是决定通过组建反对执政的塞尔维亚进步党（SNS）的联盟来接管权力，该党已经在过去14年里执政。他们组织了一个由专业人士和社会活动家组成的无党派选举名单。在2026年10月25日的议会选举中，学生联盟赢得52.7%的选票，并在国民议会250个席位中获得140席。执政党获得39.17%的选票和104席。投票率为68.78%。总统亚历山大·武契奇承认失败。然而，当欧洲学生意识到自己的责任时，世界许多地方的学生却在沉睡。在拥有世界最大黑人人口的尼日利亚，许多学生和青年实际上在打鼾，而他们国家2027年大选争夺未来的斗争已经开始。更严重的是，许多醒着的人却自愿被政客当作暴徒和雇佣的顽童使用，而那些政客的过往并非秘密。除了政客及其子女向学生强加领导人之外，曾有一段时间，全国尼日利亚学生协会（NANS）的中央主席甚至不是学生！然而，这并不意味着这样的国家不会筑起路障。当学生和青年行动起来时，社会就会发生改变。奥韦·拉肯法，前非洲工人秘书长，是一位人权活动家、记者和作家

https://www.yna.co.kr/view/akr2026110103.summary: (서울=연합뉴스) 이정현 조다운 기자 = 국민의힘 장동혁 대표는 1일 박근혜 전 대통령이 지난 달 25일 오찬에서 "좋은 인재들로 우리가 채워서 다음 총선에서 이기고 그것을 바탕으로 정권을 가져와야지만 대한민국의 시스템을 지켜낼 수 있다"고 당부했다고 전했다. 장 대표는 이날 MBN '시사스페셜 정운갑의 집중분석'에 출연해 "이재명 정권이 들어서서 대한민국의 여러 시스템이 무너지고 있는데, 우리 시장경제와 자유민주주의 시스템을 굳건히 지키기 위해서는 이런 시스템을 지키겠다는 확고한 신념을 가진 좋은 인재들로 채워야 한다고 (박 전 대통령이) 말씀을 주셨다"며 이같이 밝혔다. 장 대표는 또 "박 전 대통령께서는 당 대표로서 많은 현안을 일일이 챙기는 것도 중요하기는 한데 그래도 놓치지 말아야 할 것은, 이번 투표용지 부족 사태를 거치면서 앞으로는 이런 의혹들이 생기지 않게 선거제도를 고치는 것, 선관위를 개혁하는 문제들에 대해선 놓치지 않고 끝까지 결과를 만들어낼 수 있도록 해야 한다는 말씀을 주셨다"고 했다.

https://www.yna.co.kr/view/akr2026110103.title_zh: 张东赫：“朴槿惠提到要靠人才赢得大选并夺取政权”
https://www.yna.co.kr/view/akr2026110103.body_zh: （首尔＝韩联社）记者李正贤、曹 downed 报道称，国民力量党党首张东赫1日转述，朴槿惠前总统在25日的午餐会上嘱咐说：“我们要用优秀人才充实自己，在下一次大选中获胜，并以此为基础掌握政权，这样才能守住大韩民国的制度。”张代表当天出席MBN《时事特评：正云甲》并表示：“李在明政权上台后，大韩民国的多个制度正在崩塌。为了牢牢守住我们的市场经济和自由民主主义制度，我们必须用坚定相信并愿意守护这些制度的优秀人才充实自身。这是朴前总统告诉我们的。”张代表还说：“朴前总统告诉我们，作为党首，逐一处理许多当前议题固然重要，但仍有一件事绝不能错过：经历此次选票短缺事件后，我们必须确保今后不再发生类似疑虑，改革选举制度、改革中央选举管理委员会，对于这些问题绝不能置之不理，必须坚持到底并取得成果。”张代表最近在朴前总统抵达首尔、纪念其父亲朴正熙前总统诞辰47周年并前往陵墓参拜时，曾与其共进午餐。当时随座的行政总理郑熙用向韩联社介绍称：“朴前总统祝贺张代表成为任期最长的党首，并嘱咐他以张代表为中心好好引领政党，让国家发展，同时牵制执政党。他还表示，担忧左翼阵营对历史的歪曲正通过电影等方式被用于教育，并传达了对朝鲜挑衅地雷等当前安保局势的忧虑。报道可经KakaoTalk okjebo发送给版权所有者(c)韩联社，禁止未经许可转载、再发布及用于人工智能学习和利用。2026/11/01 16:56发稿。2026年11月1日16时56分发稿。摄影：韩联社记者李东海。高阳市＝韩联社。在京畿道高阳市 Janghangdong 小农坎于27日举行的2026年国民力量党国会议员联合恳谈会上，朴槿惠前总统与张东赫党首握手交谈。2026.8.27 eastsea@yna.co.kr

https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new.body: Weeks after Indian pilot Smit Machchhar fought off an attack by his Omani co-pilot on a Dubai-Tel Avivi flydubai flight, the identities of two off-duty pilots who took charge of the flight amid the chaos have been revealed. According to a Times of Israel report, pilots Henson Steven of Fiji and Rowan Tooth of South Africa took control of the plane after Smit Machcchhar was attacked by his co-pilot Hamam al-Hammami, who investigators said was trying to crash the plane. The flydubai crew members were awarded the First Class Order of Zayed II by UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan earlier this week but their identities were not known until then. More than 170 people were aboard the flydubai flight FZ1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv when Machchhar was attacked by his co-pilot with a crash axe. The chaos sent the jet plunging nearly 14,000 feet in less than 30 seconds. It was after an injured Machchhar managed to open the cockpit door that passengers and other crew members were alerted about the attack and successfully overpowered the co-pilot. An Israeli passenger briefly grabbed controls of the flight before the off-duty co-pilots took over. “The plane started leveling out a little more, and then the pilot told me he was taking over from there,” Israeli passenger Yaniv Hayun had said. He had also accused the co-pilot of trying to destroy controls. Pilots Steven and Tooth made an emergency landing of the flight in Saudi Arabia before a replacement plane took passengers to Tel Aviv, Times of Israel reported on Saturday. Steven reportedly previously worked for Fiji Airways and South African airline Airlink. According to a Jerusalem Post report published last month, the off-duty pilots were on board to prepare for the possibility that regional airspace restrictions could force the aircraft to take a longer route. The additional pilots were there to ensure the crew did not exceed its permitted duty hours, the report had said, citing a person familiar with the matter

https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new.body_zh: 数周前，印度飞行员Smit Machchhar在迪拜—特拉维夫的flydubai航班上击退其阿曼副驾驶发动的攻击后，两名在混乱中接管客机的非当班飞行员身份终于曝光。据《以色列时报》报道，在Smit Machcchhar遭副驾驶Hamam al-Hammami袭击后，斐济飞行员Henson Steven和南非飞行员Rowan Tooth接管了飞机；调查人员称，袭击者试图让飞机坠毁。本周早些时候，这两名flydubai机组人员获阿联酋总统谢赫穆罕默德·本·扎耶德·阿勒纳哈扬授予扎耶德二世等功勋勋章，但直到当时外界才知道他们的身份。FZ1073班机从迪拜飞往特拉维夫，机上载有170多人；Machchhar遭副驾驶用砍斧袭击后，客机在不到30秒内猛坠近14,000英尺。受伤的Machchhar设法打开驾驶舱门后，乘客和其他机组人员得知发生袭击，并成功制服了副驾驶。一名以色列乘客曾短暂握住客机操纵装置，随后两名非当班副驾驶接管了飞机。以色列乘客Yaniv Hayun曾说：“飞机开始变得更加平稳，随后飞行员告诉我，从那一刻起由他接管。”他还指控副驾驶企图破坏操纵装置。据《以色列时报》周六报道，Steven和Tooth让客机在沙特阿拉伯紧急着陆，随后由替换客机将乘客送往特拉维夫。据报道，Steven此前曾供职于斐济航空和南非航空公司Airlink。据《耶路撒冷邮报》上月发表的一篇报道，这两名非当班飞行员当时在机上，是为了应对区域空域限制可能迫使飞机延长航程的情况。报道援引一名知情人士的话说，增派的飞行员是为了确保机组人员不会超过获准执勤时数

https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/i.body: Account subscription benefits alongside Premium Stories, Editorials, Opinions and more. Unlock these with Subscription The Indian National Developmental Inclusive Alliance (INDIA) on Saturday (October 31, 2026) carried out a symbolic “public impeachment” of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, unanimously adopting a motion by a show of hands. They levelled six charges against him, including conspiring with the ruling BJP to steal elections, deleting 13.2 crore voters through the special intensive revision (SIR) of voter lists, and acting at the behest of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah. Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi described the exercise as a “political weapon” aimed at all those who had “colluded” to destroy the votes of the Indian people. He asserted that Mr. Kumar should not only be removed from office but also tried in a court of law for treason. The Opposition was compelled to hold a public impeachment because “every other institution and institutional direction” was closed to it, Mr. Gandhi said in his concluding remarks, warning that those involved in alleged electoral irregularities “would not escape accountability and would eventually have to face the representatives of the people”. The motion was initiated by Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, whose official residence at 10, Rajaji Marg, served as the venue for the proceedings. Moving the motion, Mr. Kharge levelled six charges against the CEC, alleging that he had worked under the directions of the Prime Minister and the Home Minister. The proceedings, which continued for three-and-a-half hours, were modelled on those of Parliament, replicating the setting of the Lok Sabha, with former Speaker Meira Kumar presiding over the session. Senior INDIA bloc leaders, including Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson Sonia Gandhi, occupied the front-row seats. Apart from Opposition MPs, civil society representatives, student leaders and voters who alleged that their names had been wrongfully deleted from electoral rolls during the SIR also took part in the proceedings. Mr. Gandhi said the gathering in the garden of Mr. Kharge’s residence was unprecedented and reflected the closure of institutional avenues available to the Opposition. “This may look like a meeting of MPs and ordinary citizens, but it is, in fact, a political weapon aimed directly at every single person who colluded to destroy the votes of the Indian people,” Mr. Gandhi said. “You are hiding behind the institution you have sworn to protect. Remember, you cannot hide behind it forever. One day, you will have to face the representatives of the people of this country,” he added, addressing Mr. Kumar and other officials. He claimed that the CEC will not survive in his post once the Opposition brings out all the proofs into the public domain. In a pointed warning to officials working under the CEC, Mr. Gandhi said they could not expect legal protection to shield them indefinitely. “Mr. Modi and Mr. Shah might be on top. We will deal with them, but you are their instruments, and so you are our first target,” he said. He cautioned officials not to underestimate the public response in a time of political change. “This is a warning to you: things are shifting. Please hear this warning and realise that this is a new political weapon sitting in the garden, and this weapon is going to hurt you very badly if you continue down your path,” he said. Mr. Gandhi alleged that 13.3 crore votes had been deleted from electoral rolls, accounting for nearly 15% of India’s electorate, while the difference between the Opposition and the winning side in the 2024 Lok Sabha election was only three percentage points. “13.3 crore voters were deleted. That is one in every seven Indians. 15% of India’s voters were deleted. You cannot delete 13.3 crore votes and argue that the 2024 elections were legal,” he said. Earlier, moving the motion, Mr. Kharge accused the CEC of overseeing a conspiracy to manipulate elections, deleting voters’ names, changing Form 6 without parliamentary oversight, centralising electoral rolls through ERONET/ECINET, excluding the other two Election Commissioners from decision-making, and acting at the behest of the Prime Minister and the Home Minister. “The right to vote is under threat because CEC Gyanesh Kumar is running the Election Commission on the directions of Modi and Shah,” Mr. Kharge alleged. He said 193 Opposition MPs had submitted notices in both Houses of Parliament seeking Mr. Kumar’s removal seven months ago, but their proposals had been rejected. The present exercise, he said, was intended to defend the dignity of a constitutional institution and restore public confidence in the Election Commission. “We have no personal enmity with the CEC. We want the Election Commission to work impartially and maintain the trust of the people in it,” he said, adding that that the law which gives lifelong immunity to the CEC should be repealed. “We are fighting to keep genuine voters on electoral rolls. It is the BJP which is protecting ghuspaithiyas . The pot is calling the kettle black,” the Congress chief said, rejecting the BJP’s charge that the Opposition was seeking to protect so-called ‘infiltrators’ in the electoral rolls. Trinamool Congress leader Sagarika Ghose alleged that the 2026 West Bengal Assembly election was “stolen” by deleting eligible voters from the electoral rolls, while her colleague, Mahua Moitra also claimed that 71% of those deleted from the Bengal electoral rolls were Muslims and 51% were women. CPI MP P. Sandosh Kumar said the country was witnessing a reversal of the democratic experiment undertaken during the first general election. “In a democracy, people elect the government. In SIR, the reverse is happening — the government is selecting the voters,” he said, describing the exercise as a “genocide of democracy”. Independent Rajya Sabha member Kapil Sibal described Mr. Kumar as a “pawn on a chess board,” and argued that manipluting the electoral rolls electronically came under the definition of treason under criminal laws. Other senior leaders, including former Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Mehbooba Mufti, Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Arvind Sawant, CPI(ML) MP Sudama Prasad, and the Samajwadi Party’s Harendra Malik, also spoke on the motion. 印度全国发展包容联盟（INDIA）于星期六（2026年10月31日）对首席选举专员贾内什·库马尔举行了一场象征性的“公开弹劾”。会议以举手表决方式一致通过一项动议，并提出六项指控，包括指其与执政的印度人民党（BJP）合谋窃取选举、通过选民名册特别集中修订（SIR）删除1320万选民，以及奉总理纳伦德拉·莫迪和内政部长阿米特·沙阿之命行事。

人民院反对党领袖拉胡尔·甘地称，这一行动是一种“政治武器”，矛头指向所有“勾结”破坏印度人民选票的人士。他断言，库马尔先生不仅应被免职，还应接受法院审判并承担叛国罪责任。甘地先生在总结发言中说，反对党之所以不得不举行公开弹劾，是因为“其他所有机构和制度途径”都已对其关闭；他警告，被指控存在选举违规行为的人士“不会逃脱问责，最终将不得不面对人民的代表”。

动议由国大党主席马利卡琼·卡尔格发起，其位于Rajaji Marg 10号的官邸成为活动地点。卡尔格先生提出动议时，对首席选举专员提出六项指控，称其奉总理和内政部长指示行事。活动持续三个半小时，参照议会程序设置，复刻人民院的会场安排，由前议长梅拉·库马尔主持。包括国大党议会党主席索尼娅·甘地在内的INDIA联盟资深领导人坐在前排。除反对党议员外，公民社会代表、学生领袖，以及声称自己的姓名在SIR期间被不当从选民名册中删除的选民也参加了活动。

甘地先生说，在卡尔格先生官邸花园举行的这场聚会前所未有，反映出反对党可用的制度途径已经关闭。

“这或许看起来像是议员和普通公民的聚会，但实际上，它是一件政治武器，直接针对每一个勾结破坏印度人民选票的人。”甘地先生说。

“你们躲在宣誓要保护的机构背后。记住，你们不可能永远躲在它背后。总有一天，你们将不得不面对这个国家的人民代表。”他补充说，并向库马尔先生及其他官员喊话。

他声称，一旦反对党将所有证据公之于众，首席选举专员将无法继续保住职位。甘地先生向首席选举专员下属官员发出严厉警告，称他们不能指望法律保护无限期为自身提供庇护。

“莫迪先生和沙阿先生或许身居高位。我们会处理他们，但你们是他们的工具，所以你们是我们的首要目标。”他说。

他告诫官员不要低估政治变革时期的公众反应。

“这是对你们的警告：形势正在变化。请听取这一警告，意识到花园里现在摆着一件新的政治武器；如果你们继续沿原路走下去，这件武器会让你们遭受严重打击。”他说。

甘地先生指称，有1330万张选票从选民名册中被删除，约占印度选民的近15%，而2024年人民院选举中反对党与胜选一方之间的差距仅为三个百分点。

“删除了1330万名选民，也就是每七个印度人中就有一个。印度15%的选民被删除。你们不能一边删除1330万张选票，一边辩称2024年的选举是合法的。”他说。

此前，卡尔格先生提出动议时，指控首席选举专员监管一场操纵选举的阴谋，包括删除选民姓名、在没有议会监督的情况下更改Form 6、通过ERONET/ECINET集中管理选民名册、将另外两名选举专员排除在决策之外，以及奉总理和内政部长之命行事。

“由于首席选举专员贾内什·库马尔按照莫迪和沙阿的指示管理选举委员会，投票权正受到威胁。”卡尔格先生指控说。

他说，193名反对党议员早在七个月前便已向议会两院提交通知，要求免去库马尔先生职务，但相关提案遭到否决。他说，此次行动旨在维护宪法机构的尊严，并恢复公众对选举委员会的信心。

“我们与首席选举专员没有个人恩怨。我们希望选举委员会公正履职，维护人民对它的信任。”他说，并补充称，应废除赋予首席选举专员终身豁免权的法律。

“我们是在争取让真正的选民留在选民名册中。保护非法居留者的是印度人民党（BJP）。这真是贼喊捉贼。”这位国大党主席说，驳斥了印度人民党关于反对党企图保护选民名册中所谓“渗透者”的指控。

人民党（草根国大党）领导人萨加里卡·戈什指称，2026年西孟加拉邦议会选举是通过从选民名册中删除合格选民而“偷走”的；她的同僚马胡阿·莫itra也声称，从孟加拉选民名册中被删除者有71%是穆斯林，51%是女性。

印度共产党议员P.桑多什·库马尔说，该国正在目睹首次大选期间开启的民主试验发生逆转。

“在民主制度中，人民选举政府。而在SIR中，情况却反了过来——政府挑选选民。”他说，并将这一行动称为“对民主的种族灭绝”。

印度联邦院独立议员卡皮尔·西巴尔将库马尔先生形容为“国际象棋棋盘上的一枚棋子”，并主张，通过电子手段操纵选民名册符合刑法中叛国罪的定义。

其他资深领导人也就动议发言，包括查谟和克什米尔前首席部长梅布巴·穆夫提、Shiv Sena（UBT）领导人阿温德·萨万特、印度共产党（马克思主义列宁主义）议员苏达马·普拉萨德，以及社会民主党领导人哈伦德拉·马利克。

Many supporters arrived in Delhi on Sunday (November 1, 2026) morning, while several others had reached the national capital on Saturday (October 31, 2026) or earlier as parties mobilised their cadres from different states for the protest. Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Saturday (October 31, 2026) urged people coming to Delhi for the protest to also shop from local traders ahead of Diwali, Chhath and Bhai Dooj, asserting that the Opposition's programme would not hurt businesses. In a video message posted on X, Mr. Gandhi said lakhs of people were expected to reach the capital and urged them to support small traders. "Along with protesting, marching and attending the rally tomorrow, do a little shopping too," he said, accusing the BJP of spreading rumours because it was "scared" of the Opposition's mobilisation. The 'Chalo Dilli' mobilisation will begin with a march from the Minto Road-Connaught Place junction at noon, culminating at Ramlila Maidan, where the INDIA bloc will hold a rally. Senior alliance leaders are expected to travel in open buses from Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's residence to the starting point of the march. At Ramlila Maidan, a large tricolour canopy has been erected over the main stage for senior opposition leaders, while a second stage is being arranged for representatives of the INDIA bloc state units. Rows of white canopy tents have been put up, metal barricades installed to regulate movement, and temporary platforms have been assembled. Separate entry gates and enclosures are being arranged for different categories of attendees. Organisers have also been asked to deploy volunteers to regulate the crowd, arrange drinking water and separate toilets for women, and coordinate parking with the traffic police. Overnight stay at the venue is not permitted. The INDIA bloc has said it expects a turnout of up to 10 lakh people, while Delhi Police expects around 50,000. Ramlila Maidan can accommodate 45,000 to 50,000 people when empty, but its capacity is estimated to come down to 30,000-40,000 with chairs, enclosures and designated passageways in place. More than 4,000 police personnel, along with Central Armed Police Forces companies, are being deployed for security and crowd management along the march route and at the venue. The ground has been divided into 14 zones, each supervised by an officer of assistant commissioner rank. More than 200 CCTV cameras, drones and body-worn cameras will be used for surveillance. The INDIA bloc has appealed to students, youth, women, workers and civil society members to join the protest. The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and student organisations have also extended support to the mobilisation. The mobilisation follows a symbolic 'public impeachment' of Mr. Kumar organised by the INDIA bloc at Mr. Kharge's residence on Saturday. Former Lok Sabha Speaker Meira Kumar presided over the proceedings, during which Kharge moved a resolution listing the Opposition's charges against the CEC, and Rahul Gandhi delivered the concluding remarks before it was adopted. The Opposition has been protesting against what it describes as 'vote chori', alleging large-scale deletion of voters' names during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/i.body_zh: 订阅账户福利以及高级故事、社论、观点等。使用订阅即可解锁这些内容 萨马杰瓦迪党工人在该党主席阿希莱什·亚达夫的住所外聚集，而国大党支持者团体则在喜马偕尔大厦外集合，随后前往集会地点。许多支持者于周日（2026年11月1日）上午抵达德里，而其他几批人已在周六（2026年10月31日）或更早时候到达首都，因为各党正从不同邦动员其骨干参加抗议。国大党领袖拉胡尔·甘地于周六（2026年10月31日）敦促前来德里参加抗议的人们在排灯节、恰特节和兄妹节前也从当地商贩那里购物，并坚称反对党举办的活动不会损害商业。在X平台发布的一则视频信息中，甘地先生表示预计将有数十万人抵达首都，并敦促他们支持小商贩。他说：“除了抗议、游行和参加明天的集会外，也去进行一点购物吧。”他指责印度人民党散布谣言，因为它对反对党的动员感到“害怕”。‘向德里进发’动员活动将于中午从明托路-康诺特广场交汇处开始游行，最终在拉姆利拉广场结束，印度国家发展包容联盟将在那里举行集会。联盟资深领导人预计将乘坐敞篷巴士从国大党主席马利卡琼·卡尔格的住所前往游行起点。在拉姆利拉广场，主舞台上方已搭建起一个大型三色旗顶篷，供反对党资深领导人使用，同时正在为印度国家发展包容联盟各邦单位代表安排第二个舞台。成排的白色顶篷帐篷已经搭起，安装了金属路障来规范人员流动，并组装了临时平台。正在为不同类别的与会者安排单独的入口门和围栏。组织者还被要求部署志愿者来管理人群、安排饮用水、为女性设置单独厕所，并与交通警察协调停车事宜。不允许在集会地点过夜。印度国家发展包容联盟表示预计将有多达100万人参加，而德里警方预计约有5万人。拉姆利拉广场在空旷时可容纳4.5万至5万人，但随着椅子、围栏和指定通道就位，其容量预计将降至3万至4万人。超过4000名警察人员以及中央武装警察部队分队正被部署在游行路线沿途和集会地点进行安保和人群管理。该场地已被划分为14个区域，每个区域由一名助理专员级别的官员监督。将使用超过200个闭路电视摄像头、无人机和随身摄像头进行监控。印度国家发展包容联盟呼吁学生、青年、妇女、工人和公民社会成员加入抗议。蟑螂人民党（CJP）和学生组织也对此次动员提供了支持。此次动员是在印度国家发展包容联盟于周六在卡尔格住所组织的针对库马尔先生的象征性“公众弹劾”之后进行的。前人民院议长梅拉·库马尔主持了程序，在此期间卡尔格提出了一项决议，列出了反对党对首席选举专员的指控，拉胡尔·甘地在决议通过前发表了总结性发言。反对党一直在抗议它所描述的“选票偷窃”，指控在选民名单特别密集修订（SIR）期间大规模删除选民姓名。印度选举委员会 / 联盟与联合 / 抗议 评论必须用英语，并使用完整句子。评论不得具有攻击性或涉及个人。请遵守我们的社区准则来发布您的评论。我们已迁移到新的评论平台。如果您已经是《印度教徒报》的注册用户并已登录，您可以继续与我们的文章互动。如果您没有账户，请注册并登录以发表评论。用户可以通过登录他们在Vuukle上的账户来访问他们以前的评论。

https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/foreignaffa.body: Foreign Minister Cho Hyun met separately with his German and Polish counterparts on the sidelines of a Group of 20 (G20) meeting in Atlanta to discuss ways to enhance bilateral cooperation, his office said Saturday. Cho met with German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul on Friday (U.S. time), expressing hope for deeper ties with the European nation in a wide range of areas, including defense, the economy and cutting-edge industries, according to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. In response, Wadephul thanked Seoul's foreign ministry for successfully preparing for German Chancellor Friedrich Merz's recent visit to Korea and expressed hope for expanded cooperation in bilateral trade and investment. Cho also met with his Polish counterpart, Radoslaw Sikorski, and called for continued discussions on cooperation in areas such as defense and batteries as a follow-up to Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk's visit to Korea in April, the ministry said. Sikorski also requested Korea's attention and support for Warsaw's efforts to join the G20, with Cho proposing continued consultations on the matter

https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/lifestyle/p.summary: Kim Sang-hyun, vice principal of Ilsung Women's Middle and High School, offered advice and encouragement to the students gathered in front of the platform on March 3 at Sinchon Methodist Church in western Seoul, at the school's entrance ceremony for the 2026 academic year. https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/lifestyle/p.summary_zh: 3月3日，在位于首尔西部的新村卫理公会教堂举行2026学年入学典礼期间，伊尔松女子初中和高中副校长金相贤向聚集在站台前的学生提出建议并予以鼓励，其中包括当天开始就读初中的77岁李福恺。他是一名成人学习者，属于因经济困难和教育中的性别不平等而失去上学机会的女性之一。
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/lifestyle/p.body: Kim Sang-hyun, vice principal of Ilsung Women's Middle and High School, offered advice and encouragement to the students gathered in front of the platform on March 3 at Sinchon Methodist Church in western Seoul, at the school's entrance ceremony for the 2026 academic year. The women about to become middle and high school students did not dress or look like other students. They wore hanbok, traditional Korean clothing, instead of uniforms, and not one of them looked like typical teenagers worn down by a nagging parent. Among them was 77-year-old Lee Bok-gae, who was entering middle school that morning — an adult learner, one of the women who lost their chance at school due to financial difficulties and gender inequality in education. Born the eldest of seven children, studying became an elusive dream, as she had to work while caring for her younger siblings. That same day, her granddaughter became a middle school student, too. On her way to a different school, the girl waved and called out to her, saying, "Grandmother, you're really cool. We're both middle school students now, so let's study hard together." "If this school didn't exist, I would have gone my whole life without ever easing the pain of being denied an education," Lee said. "I'm so grateful that even now I can run toward my dream. Teacher Lee Seon-jae, thank you so much." The vice principal ran most of the ceremony. The rest of the responsibilities rested on Lee Seon-jae, the principal to whom Lee Bok-gae had bowed her head. He had given his whole life to women living on the margins of the education system, and people called him the "Korean Pestalozzi," after Johann Heinrich Pestalozzi, the Swiss reformer who built schools for destitute children. On May 10, two months after that ceremony, he died. He was 90. Lee Seon-jae was born in Kaesong in 1936 and fled to Seoul during the 1951 evacuation of Seoul during the 1950-53 Korean War. Neighbors helped him through university, and in 1960, he opened a night school. Around that time, he heard that Ilsung Higher Civic School, which the children of war refugees attended, had gone a year without paying its rent and was holding classes outdoors. He went to a Korean medicine doctor he knew, someone who had already helped his night school, and asked for help. The school was not shut down. That was where his life with Ilsung began. Ten years passed. Older housewives and women factory workers began coming and going at Ilsung, a school until then attended mainly by refugees. The factory workers said they had come because reading the labels attached to clothing had made them curious about English. Their factory owners would not allow it. Pressed to choose — school or factory, one or the other — some of them stopped coming. What Lee Seon-jae built in answer was Ilsung's Sunday school, which threw its doors open on the one day the women did not report to the factory. The lives of the women he took in followed a similar path. Money was short. In the order of who got to study, they lost out to older and younger brothers, and were sent to work in the fields and the factories instead. As adults, they married into their husbands' families, and once they gave birth, child-rearing left them no time for themselves. When they had finally sent their children to university, they took up the care of aging parents and parents-in-law. That was what duty meant then. The school where the older women were welcomed was Ilsung Women's Middle and High School. It still enrolls 950 adult learners. They keep studying alongside the work that pays them — selling insurance, servicing water purifiers, cleaning buildings, working as certified care workers, keeping other people's houses. Kim Bong-ja, 67, was one of them. She graduated from the high school division of Ilsung and is now a student at Sookmyung Women's University. The day she received her diploma, she went to her parents' graves and wept. "Studying was my lifelong goal, and now every day feels like a dream," she said She thinks often about Lee Seon-jae's soybean-sprout lesson. "Teacher Lee used to encourage us by saying, 'When you study, there are plenty of times you forget things, but if you keep learning and learning, a moment comes when you shoot up all at once, like soybean sprouts in a sprouting pot,'" she said. "The teacher has gone on ahead of us, but his teaching will stay with me for the rest of my life." The students he opened the doors to were fiercely dedicated. Factory workers and housewives arrived so long before dawn that the school had to post a notice reading, "We open the doors at 7:30 a.m." Their zeal was a large part of why the school won recognition as an educational facility from the Seoul Metropolitan Office of Education in 2000 and grew into the Ilsung Women's Middle and High School of today. Some 63,000 students have reached the dream of learning in his care. Some of them came out of it with different lives altogether. Kang Hee-cheon, 68, is the clearest case. Kang spent middle school years in 1973 at Ilsung Higher Civic School, the predecessor of Ilsung Women's Middle and High School, where Lee taught abacus arithmetic. As Kang remembers him, Lee was always strict. Lee had recruited every child in Kang's class personally. He sought out children who were poor or abandoned by their parents — children of the street — talked them into it and brought them to the school himself. Lee drilled three things into his students: truthfulness, diligence and frugality. Only someone who does not deceive themselves can avoid deceiving others, he always added. Only someone who works sincerely can fulfill their use. Only someone who lives frugally can know what is precious. "Living right matters more than being smart" was his standing line, and whenever he spotted a student harboring resentment toward society and heading in a bad direction, Kang said, he went straight to the student's home and set it right. Kang remembers him as a teacher in the old sense of the word. "Teacher Lee Seon-jae was a mentor who lived out ahead of me, so I could learn how to live and follow even a little way behind him," Kang said. "He taught strictly, but he was the kind of person who would invent prizes that didn't exist just to spur his students on." "Maybe he is the person who decided the course of my life," Kang said. Kang finished Ilsung Higher Civic School under Lee, then entered university through a school-equivalency examination. Kang went on to pass the Grade 9 civil service examination, the entry-level rank, worked at the Mapo District Office and retired in 2017 as director of its safety and public administration bureau, a senior grade 4 post. Since retiring, Kang has volunteered with free meal programs for elderly people. "I chose the civil service because I wanted to be of benefit to society, the way Teacher Lee was," Kang said. "I wanted to give back what he gave me." The place Lee held open for adult learners may now disappear. In his will, he directed that the school operate only until February 2028. The Lifelong Education Act recognizes only school corporations and incorporated foundations as bodies entitled to establish a lifelong education facility, which means that once the founder steps away, the governing body has to convert into a converted entity. Conversion requires meeting a list of conditions, among them facilities and financing. In June, the school posted a petition on the National Assembly's website, asking lawmakers to amend the Lifelong Education Act to preserve the school's public service role, protect its students' right to learn and its teaching staff. The petition needed 50,000 signatures within a 30-day window. It did not get them, and it lapsed. Teachers and others at the school have asked education authorities for a public model instead — entrusting operations to a public foundation, for one — but the practical obstacles are considerable. Keeping open the school Lee had protected since 1960, a place that opened learning to women who had weathered life's hardships until they put their studies aside, now falls to the people he left behind. https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/lifestyle/p.title_zh: 女性因无法获得教育而哀悼曾帮助她们重返校园的校长
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/lifestyle/p.body_zh: 3月3日，首尔西部新教堂_METHODIST Church举行2026学年度入学仪式，聚集在讲台前的伊颂女子初中和高中副校长金相贤向学生们提出建议并给予鼓励。这些即将成为初中生和高中生的女性，既没有穿着打扮成其他学生的样子，也没有任何人看起来像被唠叨的父母磨去锐气的普通青少年。其中有77岁的李福介，当天上午她将升入初中——她是一名成年学习者，也是那些因经济困难和教育领域的性别不平等而失去求学机会的女性之一。她是七个孩子中最大的一个，出生后不得不一边工作、一边照顾弟妹，学习便成了一个难以实现的梦想。同一天，她的孙女也成了一名初中生。女孩在前往另一所学校的路上向祖母挥手并喊道：“祖母，你真酷。现在我们都是初中生了，一起努力学习吧。”“要不是有这所学校，我可能一辈子都无法缓解被剥夺教育所带来的痛苦。”李说，“能有如今这个机会奔向自己的梦想，我感激不尽。李善宰老师，非常感谢你。”副校长主持了入学仪式的大部分活动，其余事务则由校长李善宰负责，李福介曾向他低头致意。他把一生都献给了生活在教育体系边缘的女性，人们称他为“韩国的裴斯泰洛齐”，以纪念那位为贫困儿童创办学校的瑞士教育家约翰·海因里希·裴斯泰洛齐。5月10日，也就是仪式举行两个月后，他去世了，享年90岁。李善宰1936年出生于开城，朝鲜战争期间，1950年至1953年，在1951年首尔大疏散中逃到首尔。邻居们帮助他读完大学，1960年，他创办了一所夜校。大约在那时，他听说战时难民子女就读的伊颂高等公民学校已经拖欠了一年房租，正在室外上课。他去找了一位相识的韩医，此人此前已经帮助过他的夜校，并向对方求助。学校没有关闭。这正是他与伊颂相伴的人生起点。十年过去了。年长的家庭主妇和女工开始来到伊颂；在那之前，这所学校主要由难民子女就读。女工们说，她们来这里是因为看到衣服上缝的标签后，便对英语产生了好奇。厂主不允许她们上课。在必须做出选择——上学还是进厂，二者只能选其一——的情况下，有些人不再来了。李善宰为此创办了伊颂星期学校，在女工们不用去工厂上班的那一天敞开大门。他接纳的女性的人生经历也大同小异。她们手头拮据。按照谁有资格学习的顺序，她们总会输给哥哥和弟弟，随后便被送去田里劳动或进厂工作。成年后，她们嫁入丈夫的家族，一旦生育孩子，育儿便不给她们留下任何属于自己的时间。等她们终于把孩子送进大学，又要承担照顾年迈父母和公婆的责任。那时的责任就是如此。年长女性能够进入的学校，正是伊颂女子初中和高中。如今，学校仍招收950名成年学习者，她们一边工作维持生计——销售保险、维修净水器、清洁楼宇、担任持证护理员、打理他人房屋——一边坚持学习。67岁的金芳娥就是其中之一。她从伊颂高中部毕业，如今是淑明女子大学的学生。拿到毕业证书那天，她前往父母墓前哭泣。“学习是我毕生的目标，如今每一天都像做梦一样。”她说。她经常想起李善宰老师关于豆芽的课。“李老师过去常鼓励我们说：‘学习时，有很多时候你会忘记学过的东西，但只要不断学习、不断学习，总有一个瞬间，你会像发豆盆里的豆芽一样一下子长起来。’”她说，“老师先我们一步离去了，但他的教诲会伴随我一生。”那些被他敞开大门接纳的学生，学习起来极其专注。女工和家庭主妇往往天还没亮就到了，学校不得不张贴告示：“本于早上7:30开门。”她们的热忱是学校于2000年获得首尔 Metropolitan Office of Education授予教育机构认可，并发展成为今天的伊颂女子初中和高中的重要原因。在他的关怀下，约63,000名学生实现了学习的梦想，其中一些人最终过上了截然不同的人生。68岁的姜熙真是最明显的例子。1973年，姜在伊颂高等公民学校读初中；这所学校是伊颂女子初中和高中的前身，当时李善宰在那里教授珠算。姜回忆说，李总是很严格。李会亲自招收班上的每一个孩子。他四处寻找贫困儿童、被父母遗弃的孩子——街头儿童——说服他们上学，再亲自把他们带到学校。李反复向学生强调三点：诚实、勤奋和节俭。他总说，只有不欺骗自己的人，才不会欺骗别人；只有真诚工作的人，才能发挥自己的作用；只有生活节俭的人，才懂得什么是珍贵。“走正道比聪明更重要”是他常说的一句话。每当姜发现某个学生心怀对社会的不满，正走向歧途时，李都会直接去那名学生家中，纠正其方向。姜始终以传统意义上的老师来回忆他。“李善宰老师是一位走在前面、让我能够学习如何生活并至少跟随他一小步的人生导师。”姜说，“他教得很严格，但也是那种会为了激励学生而凭空想出奖品的人。”“或许正是他决定了我人生的轨迹。”姜说。姜在李善宰的教导下从伊颂高等公民学校毕业，随后通过同等学历考试进入大学。她参加并通过了9级公务员考试，即入门级职位考试，曾在麻浦区公所任职，并于2017年以安全与行政管理局长的高级4级职位退休。退休后，姜一直在老年人免费供餐项目中担任志愿者。“我选择成为公务员，是因为我希望像李老师那样为社会作出贡献。”姜说，“我想回报他给予我的一切。”李善宰为成年学习者敞开的大门，如今或许将消失。他在遗嘱中指示，学校只运营到2028年2月。《终身教育法》仅承认学校法人和公益财团法人为有权设立终身教育机构的团体，这意味着创办者一旦离世，运营主体就必须转换为另一种法人实体。转换需要满足一系列条件，其中包括设施和资金。6月，学校在国民议会网站上发布请愿书，要求议员修改《终身教育法》，以保留学校的公共服务职能，保护学生的学习权和教职员工权益。请愿需要在30天内获得50,000个签名，但最终未能达成，因此失效。学校教师和其他人士已请求教育主管部门提供一种公办模式，例如把学校运营委托给公共基金会，但实际障碍相当多。让李自1960年起一直守护的学校继续开放，让它继续为那些经历人生艰辛、直到晚年才不得不放下学习的女性提供求学机会，如今落到了他留下的人们肩上。本文来自《韩国先驱报》，它是《韩国时报》的姊妹报，由生成式人工智能系统翻译，并由《韩国时报》编辑。

https://leadership.ng/fg-tasks-nigerians.body: The Executive Vice Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of the National Agency for Science and Engineering Infrastructure (NASENI), Mr Khalil Suleiman Halilu, made the call during the distribution of solar home systems, clean cooking stoves and household support packs to 330 residents of Ondo State in Akure. Halilu said the initiative was designed to translate research and development into practical products that could improve living conditions and provide economic opportunities for Nigerians. He explained that the solar home systems would provide lighting for households, enable children to study at night and support small businesses, while the clean cooking stoves would offer more efficient cooking alternatives and reduce exposure to smoke when properly used. According to him, wider adoption of locally developed products would encourage domestic manufacturing and strengthen Nigeria’s capacity to develop solutions to its own challenges. He said “This is to promote locally produced items which brings about employment and also to have something good for our communities. He said the NASENI Sustainable Empowerment Programme had reached more than 10 states across the six geopolitical zones, with 330 men and women benefiting from the intervention in Ondo State. The NASENI chief executive added that the programme was intended to take technological innovations beyond research facilities and make them accessible to households and businesses. Also speaking, the Minister of Youth Development, Ayodele Olawande, said beneficiaries would receive additional financial support to enable them to establish or strengthen micro-businesses. Olawande said the intervention was not a political strategy but an effort to take technology-based solutions and economic opportunities to grassroots communities. In his remarks, gov. Yusuf commended Abejide for extending his empowerment programme beyond his constituency, urging other federal lawmakers to support Nigerians irrespective of their ethnic or religious backgrounds. https://leadership.ng/fg-tasks-nigerians.body_zh: 国家科学与工程基础设施局（NASENI）执行副主席兼首席执行官Khalil Suleiman Halilu先生，在阿库雷向奥 ND州330名居民分发太阳能家庭系统、清洁炊具和家居支持包时发出了这一号召。Halilu表示，该倡议旨在将研究与开发成果转化为实用产品，以改善生活条件，并为尼日利亚人提供经济机会。他解释说，太阳能家庭系统将为家庭提供照明，使儿童能够在夜间学习，并支持小型企业；正确使用时，清洁炊具可提供更高效的烹饪方式，并减少烟雾暴露。据他介绍，推广本地研发产品将鼓励国内制造，增强尼日利亚自主开发应对自身挑战解决方案的能力。他说：“这是为了推广本地生产的产品，既能带来就业，也能让我们的社区获得优质产品。”他说，NASENI可持续发展计划已覆盖全国六个地缘政治区域中的10多个州，其中330名男女在奥ND州受益于该项干预。NASENI首席执行官还表示，该计划旨在让技术创新走出研究机构，使家庭和企业都能获得这些成果。青年发展部长Ayodele Olawande也表示，受益者将获得额外财政支持，以便创办或强化微型企业。Olawande称，这项干预并非政治策略，而是旨在把基于技术的解决方案和经济机会带到基层社区。在发言中，州长Yusuf赞扬Abejide将其赋能计划延伸至选区之外，并敦促其他联邦议员不论尼日利亚人的族裔或宗教背景，都向其提供支持。他说，此类干预将促进国家团结、和平共处和经济发展。我们掌握独家优势。实时报道、突发独家新闻和独家视角将直接发送到您的手机。不要满足于过时新闻。加入LEADERSHIP NEWS WhatsApp频道，获取全天候最新动态 →

https://www.premiumtimesng.com/features-.summary: It is against this backdrop that the House of Representatives has begun consideration of a new bill seeking to regulate advance rent payments and protect tenants from what it describes as unlawful rental practices. A tenant who has paid rent in violation of the proposed 12-month limit could apply to the proposed FCT Rent Regulation and Tenants’ Protection Authority for a refund.
